source_text: Dicunt etiam baptisma non dare omnem indulgentiam peccatorum nec auferre crimina, sed radere, ut omnium peccatorum radices in mala carne teneantur.
pass_a_gloss: They also say that baptism does not give every pardon of sins nor take away crimes, but shaves them, so that the roots of all sins are held in the evil flesh.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: They also say that baptism does not grant complete forgiveness of sins or remove wrongdoing, but merely shaves it away, leaving the roots of all sins in the evil flesh.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
